content: This medication is approved for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation in adults, with a recommended dosage of 3 mg taken orally once daily. It is also indicated for the management of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults, with the same dosage of 3 mg orally once daily. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established in individuals under 18 years of age. It is contraindicated in children under 6 years of age, as nonclinical studies have shown that a single oral dose caused fatal dehydration in juvenile mice. Use in children aged 6 to less than 18 years is not recommended due to insufficient clinical data. Additionally, clinical studies have not included enough patients aged 65 years or older to determine whether they respond differently from younger patients. Therefore, dose selection in elderly patients should be approached with caution. Common side effects include diarrhea (5%), sinusitis, upper respiratory tract infections, abdominal distension, flatulence, abdominal tenderness, and elevated liver enzymes (ALT and AST). Hypersensitivity reactions, such as skin itching, hives, and rash, as well as vomiting, have also been reported. Severe diarrhea is rare but may occur; if it does, the medication should be discontinued, and the patient should be rehydrated. This medication is contraindicated in patients with known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction. There is insufficient data to assess the risks of major birth defects or miscarriage associated with this drug in humans. It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in human breast milk, but systemic absorption is negligible. When considering use during breastfeeding, the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant. This medication is a guanylate cyclase-C (GC-C) agonist. It works locally on the luminal surface of intestinal epithelial cells by increasing cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) levels. This activation stimulates the secretion of chloride and bicarbonate into the intestinal lumen, primarily through the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) ion channel, leading to increased intestinal fluid and accelerated transit. The drug has negligible systemic absorption and is expected to have minimal tissue distribution. It is metabolized into small peptides through proteolytic activity in the gastrointestinal tract. No human studies have been conducted to evaluate its pharmacokinetics. For patients with difficulty swallowing, the tablets can be crushed and administered orally with applesauce or water, or via a feeding tube. The medication may be taken with or without food. Tablets should be swallowed whole for each dose. If necessary, crushed tablets can be prepared as described above. The medication should be stored at room temperature, between 20-25°C (68-77°F), with permissible excursions to 15-30°C (59-86°F). It should be kept in a dry place and protected from moisture. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider.
